title: Shelter-in-Place Room
description: Use this list to set up and stock a room for staying inside during a chemical, radiation, or storm emergency, and to pick the right room for each threat.

sources.title: What to Do to Shelter in Place for a Chemical Emergency

items.text: Know the right room for each threat: chemical - interior room above ground with few windows; tornado - lowest floor interior; radiation - basement or center of building
Pick an interior room big enough for everyone and pets, ideally with a bathroom and few windows and vents
Learn how to shut off the furnace, air conditioning, and all fans (bath, kitchen, dryer) quickly
Pre-cut plastic sheeting (4 mil or thicker), about 6 inches (15 cm) larger than each window and vent, labeled for where it goes
At least two rolls of duct tape and scissors stored in the room
Battery or hand-crank radio to hear when it is safe
Essential medicines and a first aid kit
Flashlights with extra batteries - no candles or flames in a sealed room
Towels to wet and lay along the bottom of the door
Bucket toilet with bags and a lid
Step stool for sealing high vents
Plan who helps family members or neighbors who need help getting to the room
Know that a sealed room is for hours, not days - stay until officials give the all-clear, then air out the house
Agree as a family not to leave to pick up children - schools shelter students on their own plans
Check the room kit once a year and replace water, food, batteries, and medicines
